newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened mildly against the dollar on Thursday but closed almost unchanged against the basket of foreign currencies in very quiet trading, dealers said.
"The market was quiet today and the shekel was steady the whole day. The end of the Washington summit had no impact on trading," said one dealer.
The two-day summit was held by U.S. President Bill Clinton in attempt to defuse tensions between Israelis and Palestinians following bloody clashes last week.
"The Bank of Israel was not seen in the market and the representative rate was set at 6.97 percent below the slope," the dealer said.

The shekel can trade in a band of seven percent above or below a slope designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against a basket of currencies representing Israel's main trading partners.

The representative rate for the dollar was 3.1890 against 3.1850 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5584 shekels against 3.5581 on Wednesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8614 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8520 on Wednesday and against the mark at 2.0815 shekels per mark against 2.0941 on Wednesday.
The Bank of Israel set the representative rate early on Thursday due to the Jewish holiday of Succoth and will do so throughout the week.
In the afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1880 shekels.
